title: "WW7 genome annotation summary"
format: html
---

# Overview

This report summarizes features in the WW7 GFF3 annotation. GFF3 coordinates are 1-based and inclusive; we will account for that when calculating lengths.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

gff_columns <- c(
"seqid", "source", "type", "start", "end",
"score", "strand", "phase", "attributes"
)

gff <- readr::read_tsv(
"data/WW7_a01.gff3",
comment = "#",
col_names = gff_columns,
col_types = readr::cols(
start = readr::col_integer(),
end = readr::col_integer(),
.default = readr::col_character()
),
show_col_types = FALSE
)

glimpse(gff)
```


## Features by type

Before running the count, predict which feature types will be most common and what the table will tell us.

```{r}
feature_counts <- gff |>
  count(type, sort = TRUE)

feature_counts
```

The two most common feature types are `gene` (3363 counts) and `CDS` (3299 counts) respectively. Compared to the rest of the feature types, these two are significantly more abundant in the WW7 annotation, with the third most common type being `tRNA` (49 counts).


## CDS length distribution

Before viewing the plot, predict the approximate shape of the CDS length distribution. Do you expect most CDS features to be short, long, or concentrated around a typical length?

```{r}
cds_lengths <- gff |>
  filter(type == "CDS") |>
  mutate(length = end - start + 1)

ggplot(cds_lengths, aes(x = length)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 100, boundary = 0, color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "WW7 CDS length distribution",
    x = "CDS length (bp)",
    y = "Number of CDS features"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Upon rendering, the plot shows a right skew, telling us that CDS lengths overwhelmingly tend to be <2000 bp. 


## Most common products

Before viewing the table, predict what kinds of protein products will appear most often. Do you expect specific named proteins, or broad labels such as “hypothetical protein”?

```{r}
products <- gff |>
  mutate(product = stringr::str_match(
    attributes,
    "(?:^|;)product=([^;]*)"
  )[, 2]) |>
  filter(!is.na(product), product != "") |>
  count(product, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 20)

products
```

The most common product names are "hypothetical protein", "MFS transporter", and "ABC transporter permease". 


## Hypothetical proteins among CDS features

Before viewing the result, predict what share of CDS features will be annotated as hypothetical proteins.

```{r}
cds_products <- gff |>
  filter(type == "CDS") |>
  mutate(product = stringr::str_match(
    attributes,
    "(?:^|;)product=([^;]*)"
  )[, 2])

hypothetical_summary <- cds_products |>
  summarise(
    total_CDS = n(),
    hypothetical_CDS = sum(product == "hypothetical protein", na.rm = TRUE),
    share_percent = 100 * hypothetical_CDS / total_CDS
  )

hypothetical_summary
```

5.55% of the CDS features are annotated as hypothetical proteins, which is 183 hypothetical CDS features out of 3,299 total CDS features.
